title: Introduce environment plugin layer and parallel plan waves to speed infra CI
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We spend a large portion of infra CI time waiting on monolithic Terraform plans and serial provider initializations across hundreds of workspaces. This ticket introduces an "environment plugin" abstraction that decouples environment-specific provider bindings and networking templates from shared module logic, plus a CI change to run parallel plan waves (grouped by non-overlapping resource sets) to reduce end-to-end plan/apply latency.

Goals:
- Reduce Terraform plan + apply wall time in CI by ~40–60% for common change classes (module reshapes, subnet tweaks, parameter updates).
- Make provider upgrades safer by isolating provider pins and bootstrap actions to environment plugins.
- Decrease noisy churn in remote-state locking by grouping independent workspaces into parallel waves.
- Provide a migration path so on-call and platform teams can roll this out incrementally.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting existing modules or changing resource semantics. This is an orchestration and layering effort, not a module rewrite.

Design decisions made so far:
1) Environment plugin layer: introduce a small YAML/TF module interface (env-plugin) that contains provider blocks, KMS/assume-role wiring, and environment-specific subnet selectors. Shared modules will accept an explicit providers map and inputs from env-plugin. This keeps shared modules provider-agnostic.
2) Plan waves: CI will compute a dependency graph for the workspace using a lightweight heuristic (resource namespace prefixes + explicit "depends_on_wave" metadata). CI will schedule waves in parallel where there are no known cross-workspace dependencies. Each wave runs terraform init/plan in an isolated ephemeral runner with state locking.
3) Provider matrix: maintain a matrix of allowed provider versions per env-plugin (pinned with minimal overlap). Upgrades must be gated by the plugin version and a canary rollout.
4) Safety: every change runs a "plan-diff" verification step that validates no unintended global changes (EIP reassignments, subnet deletions) with a small rule set.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Spike: proof-of-concept env-plugin structure and sample migration for the "platform-networking" workspace (completed).
- SDK: small Go helper used by CI to compute waves and validate the plan-diff rules.
- TF surface: introduce env-plugin template and examples for prod/stage/dev.
- CI changes: modify infra pipeline to accept wave manifests and run waves in parallel with limited concurrency (configurable per org).
- Rollout: migrate three low-risk workspaces (dev-platform, staging-analytics, infra-tooling) to env-plugin + waves as canaries.

Migration plan:
Phase 0 (spike) — complete: validated approach against a test workspace.
Phase 1 (canary) — in progress: migrate dev-platform and staging-analytics. Monitor plan durations, state lock contention, and failure modes for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (gradual) — next: migrate medium-risk workspaces after canary signoff; adjust wave heuristic.
Phase 3 (complete) — final: update docs, deprecate legacy bootstrap scripts, and add a migration helper script.

Rollout metrics to track:
- median plan time per workspace
- 95th percentile end-to-end pipeline time
- remote-state lock wait time and lock contention events
- failed apply rate during rollout

Risk analysis and mitigations:
- State drift / race conditions: mitigate by conservative default concurrency (2–4 waves max) and strict locking. Add state snapshotting before first apply during a workspace migration.
- Provider incompatibility: require a provider smoke test harness for each env-plugin. Provider upgrades are gated behind the provider matrix and a security review.
- CI complexity: fallback path to run classic serial plan for any workspace flagged with "legacy=true".

Acceptance criteria:
- Two production-adjacent workspaces migrated with >=35% reduction in total plan/apply time and no increase in failed applies.
- CI exposes a wave-level dashboard with timings and lock contention alerts.
- Runbook updated and team training completed (platform-eng).

Notes and related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/infra/env-plugin-design (internal)
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-env-plugin (PRs linked below)
- Spike results dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/dashboards/terraform-plan-waves
comments: 2025-01-22 - Maya Patel: Spike complete. Verified that extracting provider blocks into a small env-plugin reduces duplicate provider inits across modules in local testing. Attached initial profiling data to the design doc.
2025-01-28 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented the first CI wave scheduler prototype (golang). Basic heuristic groups workspaces by resource namespace prefixes. Running batch tests now.
2025-02-05 - Priya Singh: Security flagged provider pinning policy — we need a short security review to approve the provider matrix approach. Filed SEC-1432 for tracking.

2025-02-12 - Platform QE (Daniel Kim): Performance tests: dev-platform plan time dropped from 7m20s to 4m15s when run in wave mode. Still validating apply flakiness. Added an automated snapshot step prior to first apply.

2025-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Load test across 24 simulated workspaces shows ~40% median pipeline time reduction and 2x reduction in lock wait events. Noting two edge cases where shared global resources required explicit wave sequencing.
2025-03-02 - Maya Patel: Waiting on SEC-1432 signoff for provider upgrade gating. We can continue canary migrations for non-provider changes while security review completes.
